opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: Thanks for making time, Yuki. I'm a researcher with the Work Futures Panel, an independent group that studies how people see changes at work, and nothing you tell me will be linked to your name.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: Okay. Thanks for keeping it anonymous. I get a bit nervous about this stuff, so sorry if I ramble.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Picture this. AI stays a handy tool, like a better search engine. Hiring, pay and prices carry on the way they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say it's already changing my job, even if it's 'just a tool'. The chatbot takes about a third of our calls now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Even this version isn't great for me. The tool keeps getting better at what I do, and they don't need a person for a simple bill question. I'm only safe until the next upgrade.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do in the first year? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Start looking at night courses. Something like bookkeeping or admin in a hospital. Try to save even a little, which is hard with my rent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy. Even the calm version doesn't feel calm.

S0.say: It's already changing my job. The chatbot takes about a third of our calls.
S0.think: Even this version isn't great for me. I'm only safe until the next upgrade.
S0.do: Looks into night courses like bookkeeping or hospital admin, and tries to save a little.
S0.feel: Even the calm version doesn't feel calm.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now picture this. Very capable AI exists, but it spreads slowly, over ten years or more. Some tasks disappear, but few whole jobs do. Companies hire fewer beginners. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say companies should still hire young people. You can't pull the ladder up behind you.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'm basically a beginner. Fewer beginner jobs means if I lose this one, there's nothing to step into. Ten years sounds slow, but my kind of call is the easy task they'd automate first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do in the first year? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Apply for a complaints role or team lead, the harder calls the bot can't handle. Actually start a night course, not just look at one.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious. Like I'm on a timer.

S1.say: Companies should still hire young people. You can't pull the ladder up behind you.
S1.think: My calls are the easy task they'd automate first, and there'd be no beginner job to step into.
S1.do: Applies for complaints or team lead roles and starts a night course.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Next one. Within 5 years, AI assistants that can act on their own handle most routine office work. There are layoffs and pay pressure in office jobs. Some new AI-related jobs appear, and politicians argue loudly about what to do. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say this is a choice companies are making, not the weather. They should share the savings, and we need stronger unions and a real safety net. I'd post about it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: That's my job gone. Routine office work is exactly what I do. And people like me don't have savings to ride it out.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do in the first year? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Look for a new job straight away while I still have one. Sign up for any free retraining. Ask my flatmate if we can find somewhere cheaper. Join whatever campaign is pushing for a basic income.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Sick to my stomach. I'd barely sleep.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The card mentioned new AI-related jobs. Do you see yourself in one?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Maybe? I don't know what they'd want. Probably people with degrees. I'd try anyway.

S2.say: This is a choice companies are making, not the weather. Share the savings and build a real safety net.
S2.think: That's my job gone, and people like me don't have savings to ride it out.
S2.do: Job hunts straight away, signs up for free retraining, looks for cheaper rent and joins a basic income campaign.
S2.feel: Sick to her stomach. Barely sleeping.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now a faster version. Within 2 to 3 years, AI matches skilled professionals at most thinking work. Lots of office and professional workers lose their jobs. Share and house prices boom. There's a political crisis over who should get the gains. Physical jobs are mostly untouched. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say it's obscene that share prices boom while people lose everything. Tax the gains. I'd be at the protests.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd lose my job, and so would everyone I'd be up against for the next one. There'd be thousands of us. Rent goes up with the boom. I don't see where I land.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do in the first year? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Take any job I can get. A café, a shop, a warehouse. Find a cheaper room, even far out. Go to every protest.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Panicked. Like there's no exit.

S3.say: It's obscene that share prices boom while people lose everything. Tax the gains.
S3.think: I'd lose my job along with thousands like me, and rent goes up. I don't see where I land.
S3.do: Takes any café, shop or warehouse job she can get, finds a cheaper room and goes to protests.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Last one. Everything in the previous picture happens, and on top of that, general-purpose robots arrive in warehouses, kitchens, building sites, farms and care homes within 3 to 5 years. Hands-on work is no longer a safe place to be. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Same as before, louder. Tax the gains and pay people, now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In the last one, my backup was a physical job. Café, warehouse, care work. If robots take those too, there's no backup at all. I'd be one of millions with nothing to offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do in the first year? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Honestly, I don't know. Apply for every support scheme going. Pool money with friends. Keep protesting, because it's the only thing that might change anything.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Hopeless. Even the backup plan is gone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: You said protesting is the only thing that might change anything. Do you believe it would?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have to. Otherwise I'm just waiting.

S4.say: Tax the gains and pay people, now.
S4.think: My backup was a physical job. If robots take those too, there's no backup at all.
S4.do: Applies for every support scheme, pools money with friends and keeps protesting.
S4.feel: Hopeless. Even the backup plan is gone.
